comps: 150 total: three pieces 30 each, scales and arpeggios 21, sight-reading 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each component is not required).

Choose one piece from each of Lists A (faster, agile), B (lyrical, expressive) and C (varied styles). Duets allowed for one piece at Initial-Grade 3 (primo/secondo part specified; own partner, no recorded parts). Listed editions mandatory for arrangements/transcriptions only. Memory optional (no extra marks). Repeats generally omitted unless very short; da capo/dal segno observed. Exam components may be taken in any order.

Repertoire lists are the same as ABRSM Performance Grades; switching between Practical and Performance Grades within a grade is not permitted. Digital pianos allowed at Private Visits if full-size weighted keys and sustaining pedal.
sections: Scales & technical work

Scales: C major; D minor (natural, harmonic or melodic), 1 oct, hands separately. Contrary motion: C major, a 5th, hands starting on tonic. Arpeggios: C major, D minor, a 5th (5-note pattern), hands separately. All legato, even notes, from memory, no pedal. Approx speeds: scales crotchet=54, arpeggios 52.
Sight-reading
4 bars, 4/4; C major, D minor; each hand separately in 5-finger position (tonic to dominant); legato/staccato, f and p; 30 sec to look over.
Aural & other tests
A clap pulse of a played piece; B clap back rhythm of two 2-bar phrases; C sing back two 1-bar echoes (major, tonic-mediant); D one feature question (dynamics or articulation).

sections: Scales & technical work

sections: Scales & technical work

Scales hands together, four octaves, min q=120, f/mf/p legato or staccato: Bb and D major; Bb and D minor (harmonic and melodic); chromatic similar from Bb and D; chromatic contrary from Eb (two octaves); C major in 3rds, hands separately, one octave, q=60. Arpeggios four octaves, min q=100: Bb, D major; Bb, D minor; diminished 7ths from Bb and D; dominant 7ths in Bb and D. Exercises: prepare 3 (one each from tone/balance/voicing, coordination, finger & wrist strength groups); candidate picks one, examiner one of the other two; music may be used (digital: choose any 2 from different groups).

Sight reading approx 2 grades lower, 30 s prep. F# and C minor, modulation; pedalling required.
Aural & other tests

Sight reading plus aural or improvisation (10 each). Aural (8-bar harmonised major): time signature, comment on dynamics and articulation, two other characteristics, modulation (subdominant/dominant/relative minor), locate two melody changes. Improv: 16 bars, F#/C minor, chords incl. 7ths.

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Piano 2027 & 2028 lists, valid from 1 Jan 2027 (the 2025 & 2026 lists can still be used until 31 Dec 2027). Scales, sight-reading and aural shown here are from the 2025 & 2026 syllabus; check the new syllabus for any changes. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three pieces 30 each, scales and arpeggios 21, sight-reading 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each component is not required).

Choose one piece from each of Lists A (faster, agile), B (lyrical, expressive) and C (varied styles). Duets allowed for one piece at Initial-Grade 3 (primo/secondo part specified; own partner, no recorded parts). Listed editions mandatory for arrangements/transcriptions only. Memory optional (no extra marks). Repeats generally omitted unless very short; da capo/dal segno observed. Exam components may be taken in any order.

Repertoire lists are the same as ABRSM Performance Grades; switching between Practical and Performance Grades within a grade is not permitted. Digital pianos allowed at Private Visits if full-size weighted keys and sustaining pedal.
sections: Scales & technical work

Scales: C major; D minor (natural, harmonic or melodic), 1 oct, hands separately. Contrary motion: C major, a 5th, hands starting on tonic. Arpeggios: C major, D minor, a 5th (5-note pattern), hands separately. All legato, even notes, from memory, no pedal. Approx speeds: scales crotchet=54, arpeggios 52.
Sight-reading
4 bars, 4/4; C major, D minor; each hand separately in 5-finger position (tonic to dominant); legato/staccato, f and p; 30 sec to look over.
Aural & other tests
A clap pulse of a played piece; B clap back rhythm of two 2-bar phrases; C sing back two 1-bar echoes (major, tonic-mediant); D one feature question (dynamics or articulation).

exams.name: ARSM
exams.full: Associate of the Royal Schools of Music — ABRSM Level 4 Diploma in Music Performance
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 5), about the end of the first year of an undergraduate course; 90 credits, 54 GLH, 900 TQT
comps: A pass at Grade 8 on the same or a closely related instrument: ABRSM Practical or Performance Grade 8, or an accepted equivalent from another board (for example Trinity, LCM, MTB, Guildhall, RIAM, AMEB or UNISA). No theory prerequisite.

Face-to-face (public venue or private visit) OR digital (video recorded at a time and place of the candidate's choice, with no fixed sessions; video uploaded at booking or within 28 days). Performance only: 30-minute programme (±2 min), timed from the first note to the last. Marks: pieces 30 (60%) + performance as a whole 20 (40%) = 50. Distinction 45–50, Merit 40–44, Pass 34–39, Below Pass 17–33.

At least 20 minutes from the ARSM repertoire list for the instrument, plus up to 10 minutes of own-choice music at Grade 8 standard or above. No written or spoken elements and no other tests (no viva, no programme notes, no quick study). Candidates submit a programme form, or enter programme details online for digital exams.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ARSM repertoire list for piano, read from the ABRSM PDF (161 entries). Works are to be performed complete unless a selection is specified (e.g. 'any two'). Refer to the qualification specification for programming requirements. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

Pathway as of Oct 2026: ARSM (L4) → LRSM (L6) → FRSM (L7). DipABRSM is withdrawn (last date 31 Dec 2023). The old-format LRSM closed 30 Apr 2024 and the old FRSM closed 31 Oct 2024. All three current diplomas require only Grade 8 in the instrument (ABRSM or an equivalent board for LRSM/FRSM). No Grade 5 or 6 theory prerequisite is stated for any current performance diploma. Under the old syllabus, Grade 5 theory appeared only as a condition on some substitutions. ARSM has no written element. LRSM/FRSM need a written (2,000 / 3,500 words) or spoken-video (10 / 17 min) supporting-evidence submission. Digital exams have no fixed sessions: book, pay and upload any time; for digital ARSM the video goes in at booking or within 28 days. Specific LRSM/FRSM upload windows weren't stated in the spec, which refers to abrsm.org/how-to-book. ABRSM discontinued printed diploma syllabuses, and lists are updated online, so re-check the abrsm.org pages before entering. abrsm.org HTML pages returned redirect errors to the fetch tool, so some details come from the PDFs and ABRSM's Taiwan mirror.
General rules (all instruments)

Both LRSM and FRSM programmes must be balanced and varied: a variety of moods, keys and tempi and at least two pieces or movements contrasting by period or style. Works and movements must be played complete unless the repertoire list says otherwise, and any list-specific instructions must be followed. Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.

exams.name: FRSM
exams.full: Fellowship of the Royal Schools of Music — ABRSM Level 7 Diploma in Music Performance
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 7, about master's/postgraduate level; 134 GLH, 2250 TQT, 225 credits
comps: Same as LRSM: Grade 8 (or equivalent, or approved professional experience) in the instrument presented. LRSM is NOT a formal prerequisite under the new spec.

Digital only. Continuous-take video recital of 55 min ±10%. Woodwind may take one break of up to 5 min. Marks and bands are the same as LRSM: 30/30/15 = 75; Distinction 68–75, Merit 60–67, Pass 50–59.

At least 50% from the FRSM list; own choice up to 50% (about 27 min) at or beyond LRSM standard. Unit 2 supporting evidence (same four options; analysis option covers a 30-min section): 3,500 words ±10% written OR a 17-min ±10% spoken video. No viva voce and no quick study.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official FRSM repertoire list for piano, read from the ABRSM PDF (106 entries). Works are to be performed complete unless otherwise specified; where a choice such as "any one or two" is shown, it applies to that work or group of pieces. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

Pathway as of Oct 2026: ARSM (L4) → LRSM (L6) → FRSM (L7). DipABRSM is withdrawn (last date 31 Dec 2023). The old-format LRSM closed 30 Apr 2024 and the old FRSM closed 31 Oct 2024. All three current diplomas require only Grade 8 in the instrument (ABRSM or an equivalent board for LRSM/FRSM). No Grade 5 or 6 theory prerequisite is stated for any current performance diploma. Under the old syllabus, Grade 5 theory appeared only as a condition on some substitutions. ARSM has no written element. LRSM/FRSM need a written (2,000 / 3,500 words) or spoken-video (10 / 17 min) supporting-evidence submission. Digital exams have no fixed sessions: book, pay and upload any time; for digital ARSM the video goes in at booking or within 28 days. Specific LRSM/FRSM upload windows weren't stated in the spec, which refers to abrsm.org/how-to-book. ABRSM discontinued printed diploma syllabuses, and lists are updated online, so re-check the abrsm.org pages before entering. abrsm.org HTML pages returned redirect errors to the fetch tool, so some details come from the PDFs and ABRSM's Taiwan mirror.
General rules (all instruments)

Both LRSM and FRSM programmes must be balanced and varied: a variety of moods, keys and tempi and at least two pieces or movements contrasting by period or style. Works and movements must be played complete unless the repertoire list says otherwise, and any list-specific instructions must be followed. Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.
Other components

Unit 2 is a written submission (3500 words, plus or minus 10%, PDF) or a spoken video presentation (17 minutes, plus or minus 10%) on one of four options: Informing your audience, Detailed analysis, Programming your performance, or Preparation for performance, based on substantial personal research and reflection. Same format, translation/subtitle and declaration rules as LRSM. First page of each own-choice piece is uploaded as PDF.

exams.syllabus: RQF Level 6, about the final year of an undergraduate degree; 108 GLH, 1800 TQT, 180 credits
comps: ABRSM Grade 8 (Practical or Performance), or an equivalent Grade 8 from a listed awarding body, in the instrument presented (a closely related instrument is accepted). Approved professional experience can substitute (approval takes up to 6 weeks and must be granted before entry). No age limits. ARSM is NOT a formal prerequisite. The new spec only requires Grade 8.

Digital only, available since April 2024. Video of a live recital recorded in one continuous take, unpaused, in a venue of the candidate's choice, with or without an audience; under-18s need a responsible adult. Performance 45 min ±10%. Woodwind may take one break of up to 4 min. Marks: Unit 1 pieces 30 (40%) + performance as a whole 30 (40%); Unit 2 supporting evidence 15 (20%); total 75. Distinction 68–75, Merit 60–67, Pass 50–59. Candidates don't need to pass every component.

At least 50% of programme time from the LRSM list; own choice up to 50% (about 22 min) at or beyond ARSM standard (solo, chamber or ensemble works, own compositions or arrangements). Unit 2 supporting evidence: one option from Informing your audience / Detailed programme analysis (a 20-min section) / Programming your performance / Preparation for performance, as 2,000 words ±10% written OR a 10-min ±10% spoken video. No viva voce and no quick study.

exams.name: ATCL
exams.full: Associate of Trinity College London (Music Performance)
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 4/5); Ofqual qualification no. 600/0949/4
comps: None formal: no minimum age, no prior grade or theory qualification required.

Available face-to-face (at Trinity centres, no audience) and digital (one continuous unedited video, max 3GB, uploaded with written programme, any approval letter and one scan per piece; audience allowed). Same structure, criteria and certificate in both formats. Recital 32-38 min performing time (exam slot 40 min). Marked out of 100: Recital 96 (Fluency & accuracy 32, Technical assurance & application 32, Musical sense & communication 32) + Programme & planning 4 (written programme 2, planning/balance/construction 2). Results: Distinction 80-100, Pass 60-79, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No Merit band.

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. Accompanied candidates may include unaccompanied works up to 40% of the programme. No viva/discussion component is mentioned in the March 2026 syllabus. Written programme (composers, titles, timings) required; no full programme notes at ATCL. Trinity describes ATCL as equivalent to a first-year undergraduate recital.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ATCL repertoire list for piano, read from the Trinity PDF (241 entries). Programmes must have a minimum of two works, performed complete except where single movements are specified; may combine list pieces with pre-approved own-choice pieces or be all own choice. Performance durations: ATCL 32-38 min, LTCL 37-43 min, FTCL 42-48 min. Piano concertos (FTCL only) need a second piano for the orchestral reduction, max one concerto-style work; an acoustic piano must be used (no digital pianos). Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Short programmes may be penalised.com resource IDs were mis-identified by the fetch tool, but every list used here was confirmed by its heading and by at least two consistent fetches.
General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction of the programme (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required at ATCL.

exams.name: LTCL
exams.full: Licentiate of Trinity College London (Music Performance)
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 6 (EQF 6); Ofqual qualification no. 600/0984/6
comps: None formal (ATCL is not required first); no grade or theory prerequisite.

Available face-to-face (at Trinity centres, no audience) and digital (one continuous unedited video, max 3GB, uploaded with written programme, any approval letter and one scan per piece; audience allowed). Same structure, criteria and certificate in both formats. Recital 37-43 min performing time (exam slot 45 min). Same 100-mark scheme as ATCL (96 recital + 4 programme & planning). Distinction 80-100, Pass 60-79.

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. Accompanied candidates may include unaccompanied works up to 40% of the programme. No viva/discussion component is mentioned in the March 2026 syllabus. Written programme required. Trinity describes LTCL as equivalent to a final-year undergraduate recital.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official LTCL repertoire list for piano, read from the Trinity PDF (307 entries). Programmes must have a minimum of two works, performed complete except where single movements are specified; may combine list pieces with pre-approved own-choice pieces or be all own choice. Performance durations: ATCL 32-38 min, LTCL 37-43 min, FTCL 42-48 min. Piano concertos (FTCL only) need a second piano for the orchestral reduction, max one concerto-style work; an acoustic piano must be used (no digital pianos). Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Short programmes may be penalised.com resource IDs were mis-identified by the fetch tool, but every list used here was confirmed by its heading and by at least two consistent fetches.
General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required. Learning outcomes add contextual understanding and the candidate's own musical voice.

p0349.d: Piatigorsky's virtuoso arrangement of the Ritual Fire Dance: relentless driving rhythm building to a wild ending.

p0390.d: Gardel's famous tango song: a sweeping, nostalgic melody over insistent tango rhythm.

p0709.d: Arrangement of Ravel's Pavane: a slow, stately, melancholy melody over gentle harmonies. Demands a beautifully controlled singing line rather than technical display.

s0045.d: Arrangement of Albéniz's famous Tango in D from España. Elegant habanera rhythm, sultry phrasing and rubato.

s0976.d: Arrangement of the stately Menuet from Handel's Royal Fireworks Music; a dignified triple-time dance practising steady pulse, clear articulation and shaped phrases.

s1698.d: Petzold's Minuet in G minor (BWV Anh. 115) from the Anna Magdalena Bach notebook: a graceful, slightly melancholy minuet. Practises phrasing, light articulation and steady triple time.

s0206.d: An arrangement of the jazz standard 'Fly Me to the Moon' (1954), made famous by Frank Sinatra. Gentle swing and smooth phrasing.
s0206.rw: Classic standard; great for jazz feel

s1947.d: Arrangement of the 1940 wartime ballad by Manning Sherwin and Eric Maschwitz. A wistful, crooning song melody with jazzy harmonies; needs warm tone, flexible phrasing and stylish rubato.
s1947.rw: Nostalgic standard; shows tone and style

s2103.d: A short arrangement of a Telemann gavotte: a cheerful, poised duple-time Baroque dance practising clear articulation.

s0673.d: Debussy's early piano Rêverie in D flat: a dreamy, floating melody over rocking harmonies; needs soft sustained tone, rubato and careful pedalling.

s0675.d: Debussy's languorous slow waltz; sensuous, rubato-laden phrases and café-style charm requiring fine tonal control.

s0746.d: Arrangement of the Ellington–Strayhorn jazz standard 'Satin Doll' (1953): a cool, laid-back swing melody with syncopation and stylish phrasing.
s0746.rw: Classic jazz tune; stylish and appealing

s0809.d: Arrangement of the haunting waltz 'Once Upon a December' from the film Anastasia: a wistful 3/4 melody. Practises smooth legato phrasing and flowing triple time.

s0861.d: Gershwin's second Prelude (1926): slow, bluesy 'lullaby' in C sharp minor with smoky melody over a walking bass; needs relaxed rhythm and rich voicing.

w00046.d: Tender piece from a children's album by a French woman composer. Practises gentle legato and sensitive phrasing.

w03125.d: Massenet's well-known Mélodie (Élégie), originally for piano: a sorrowful C minor song over steady accompaniment; trains cantabile, voicing and pedalling.

w03505.d: Energetic Ukrainian dance with a stamping, bouncy rhythm; practises hand coordination and rhythmic drive at the very first level.

w03506.d: Short fanfare-like piece with royal, march-like character and bold dynamics; practises steady rhythm and simple hand coordination.

w03507.d: Swedish folk tune about a sleeping bear, arranged simply with a slow, quiet melody; practises smooth legato and soft dynamics.

w03508.d: Easy arrangement of Coldplay's 2002 hit, built on the repeating piano riff; practises steady rhythm and pattern work.

w03509.d: Gentle descriptive piece imitating raindrops with light detached notes; practises touch and controlled soft playing.

w03510.d: Simple arrangement of a Diabelli piece in Turkish style, with lively march-like rhythm and short phrases; practises articulation.

w03511.d: Primo part of a Diabelli duet scherzo, with a light playful melody in simple rhythms; practises steady pulse and duet ensemble.

w03512.d: Short, tuneful dance from Gurlitt's Little Concerto album, in a simple Romantic style; practises phrasing and light touch.

w03513.d: Charming toy-character piece depicting a doll from the Black Forest, with simple staccato and legato contrasts; practises touch.

w03514.d: Short, playful scherzo with lively staccato and a bouncy melody; practises articulation and rhythm in a Soviet-era style.

w03515.d: Primo part of a lively duet with a rock-style groove; practises rhythmic control and ensemble playing.

x00420.d: Copland's The Cat and the Mouse, a witty descriptive scherzo with sneaky chromatic motifs.

x00421.d: Debussy's Suite bergamasque, with Prélude, Menuet, Clair de lune and Passepied; choose any one.

x00422.d: Debussy's Feuilles mortes (Dead leaves), a melancholy, expressive and mysterious piece.

x00426.d: Debussy's The Wine Gate, a Spanish-flavoured habanera with sultry rhythms.

x00431.d: Gershwin's Preludes: jazzy character pieces with blues and Latin flavours; any two.

x00432.d: Gershwin's jazz songs in virtuoso piano arrangements, 'The Man I Love' and 'I Got Rhythm'.

x00433.d: Ginastera's Rondo on Argentine Folk Tunes, with rhythmic vitality and folk melodies.

x00434.d: Gorb's Brahms and Red Wine, a witty contemporary piece with Brahms-like gestures.

x00435.d: Gorb's The Girl with the White Parasol, a nostalgic contemporary character piece.

x00436.d: Haydn's F minor Variations, an intense double-variation set of dignity and depth.

x00437.d: Haydn's A flat Sonata, with lyrical beauty and wit.

x00438.d: Haydn's C major Sonata Hob. XVI/48: a spacious two-movement work, an expressive Andante con espressione and a brilliant Rondo finale.

x00439.d: Haydn's E flat Sonata, a gracious sonata with a lyrical Adagio and playful finale.

x00440.d: Fanny Hensel's Abschied von Rom, a farewell reflection with rich Romantic harmony.

x00441.d: Hindemith's Interludium (Pastorale) and Fuga No. 3 from Ludus Tonalis, with a contemplative pastorale and a clear fugue.

x00442.d: Hisaishi's Merry-Go-Round of Life from Howl's Moving Castle, a waltz with beautiful, nostalgic melody.

x00443.d: Howells's Summer Idylls, a suite of seven short, atmospheric pieces.

x00444.d: Ireland's The Island Spell, an evocative Impressionist piece from Decorations.

x00445.d: Ireland's Greenways, a set of three pieces in a pastoral, English style.

x00446.d: Janáček's In the Mists, rhapsodic moody pieces with Moravian inflections.

x00447.d: Karl Jenkins's Quirky Blue, a jazz-blues influenced piece with groovy rhythms.

x00448.d: Kapustin's Big Band Sounds, a jazz showpiece for piano with fiery big-band textures.

x00449.d: Kapustin's Daybreak, a swinging jazz-based piece with flowing lines.

x00450.d: Kashperova's Murmuring of the Rye, a delicate and atmospheric Russian Romantic piece.

x00451.d: Kay's Two Impromptus, No.2, a contemporary jazzy-lyrical piece.

x00452.d: Lee's The Sun is Rising, a contemporary piece with bright rising figures.

x00453.d: Kang Ning Lim's Flower Visages, an atmospheric contemporary piece with Asian colours.

x00454.d: Liszt's Petrarch Sonnets, lyrical Italianate pieces from the Années de pèlerinage; Sonnet 47 or 123.

x00455.d: Liszt's Liebestraum No. 2, a nocturnal song with lyrical melody.

x00456.d: Makholm's 3 Impressions, atmospheric pieces in a modern style.

x00457.d: McCabe's Five Bagatelles, contrasting miniatures in a modern idiom.

x00458.d: Mendelssohn's F minor Prelude and Fugue, a dramatic and serious work in Bachian style.

x00459.d: Messiaen's Regard de l'étoile, a mystical and colourful piece from the Vingt regards.

x00460.d: Messiaen's Regard de la vierge, a serene and radiant movement with luminous textures.

x00461.d: Messiaen's Rondeau, a short, early rhythmic virtuoso piece.

x00462.d: Mozart's B minor Adagio, a profoundly expressive and chromatic work.

x00463.d: Mozart's Durnitz Sonata in D, with lively variation finale and dancing charm.

x00464.d: Mozart's C major Sonata, a charming and classical work with a singing Andante.

x00465.d: Mozart's D major Sonata K. 311: a sparkling Allegro con spirito, an expressive Andante con espressione and a lively Rondeau; trains clean passagework and Classical style.

x00466.d: Mozart's K. 455 variations on a Gluck aria, with witty and varied character.

x00467.d: Mozart's Duport Minuet variations, a bright and brilliant final set.

x00468.d: Mulsant's Le Jardin du Poète, a colourful, poetic contemporary piece.

x00469.d: Önaç's Beauty of the Bride, a lyrical contemporary piece.

x00470.d: Lawson's Song of the Autumn Lady's Tresses Orchid, a lyrical contemporary character piece.

x00471.d: Philip Martin's Broadway Boogie, a jazzy and rhythmic piece with swing rhythm.

x00472.d: Philip Martin's New York Nights, a jazz scherzo with sophisticated rhythms.

x00473.d: Poulenc's Trois Mouvements perpétuels, delicate, ironic and subtly shaded miniatures.

x00474.d: Poulenc's Toccata, a vigorous and rhythmic movement from Trois pièces.

x00475.d: Prokofiev's Visions fugitives, a selection of four of twenty delicate and witty pieces.

x00476.d: Rachmaninov's Prelude in E flat, flowing with a lyrical melodic line.

x00477.d: Rachmaninov's C minor Prelude, a stormy and dramatic piece.

x00478.d: Rachmaninov's G major Prelude, a famous flowing piece with a dreamy melody.

x00479.d: Rachmaninov's G sharp minor Prelude, expressive with a heartfelt tune.

x00480.d: Ravel's Le tombeau de Couperin, graceful neo-Baroque suite; choose two excluding Toccata.

x00481.d: Ravel's Sonatine, a classic three-movement French work with grace and brilliance.

x00482.d: Ravel's Pavane pour une infante défunte, a slow, elegant and poignant dance.

x00483.d: Roxburgh's Moonscape, an atmospheric contemporary piece.

x00484.d: Ruiz's Micro-suite, a short suite of contrasting miniatures.

x00485.d: Rhian Samuel's A Garland for Anne, a delicate contemporary piece.

x00486.d: Rhian Samuel's Distant Fountains from Dream-Images, a shimmering piece.

x00487.d: Scarlatti's Sonatas in A, K.208 and K.209, a graceful lyrical pair.

x00488.d: Scarlatti's Sonatas in G, K.259 and K.260, a brilliant and lively pair.

x00489.d: Scarlatti's E minor and E major sonatas, a contrasting pair.

x00490.d: Scarlatti's C major Sonatas, K.308 and K.309, a bright and lively pair.

x00491.d: Schoenberg's Six Little Piano Pieces, short, aphoristic atonal miniatures.

x00492.d: Schonthal's Toccata and Arietta, a contrasting brief toccata and a lyrical arietta.

x00493.d: Schubert's Impromptus Op. 90, flowing and lyrical pieces; choose any one.

x00494.d: Schubert's B flat Impromptu, a theme and variations with charm.

x00495.d: Schubert's A minor Sonata D. 537, a lyrical and graceful early sonata.

x00496.d: Schubert's A major Sonata D. 664, a sunny and lyrical sonata.

x00497.d: Clara Schumann's Romance No.1, a lyrical and tender piece.

x00498.d: Schumann's Blumenstück, a flowing floral piece with delicate variation.

x00499.d: Schumann's Des Abends and Aufschwung, a famous pair from Phantasiestücke.

x00500.d: Schumann's Novellette in F, a rhythmic and vigorous work.

x00501.d: Schumann's Romanze in B major, Op. 28 No. 3: a tender, flowing romance with a gently animated middle section.

x00502.d: Scriabin's Impromptu in B flat minor, a mazurka-like early piece.

x00503.d: Scriabin's 24 Preludes, brief and varied pieces; choose any two.

x00504.d: Sculthorpe's Night Pieces, atmospheric Australian miniatures.

x00505.d: Shostakovich's 24 Preludes, short witty and varied; choose a pair as listed.

x00506.d: Soler's Sonata No. 45 in G, a bright harpsichord-style sonata.

x00507.d: Stravinsky's Tango, a stylised and witty dance.

x00508.d: Szymanowski's Etude in B flat minor, a famous lush and expressive study.

x00509.d: Tailleferre's Sicilienne, a graceful, lilting French piece.

x00510.d: Turina's Cinco danzas gitanas, Spanish gypsy dances with rhythm and colour; choose two.

x00511.d: Wang's Glowing Red Morningstar Lillies, a Chinese-style lyrical piece.

x00512.d: Wang's Silver Clouds Chasing the Moon, a Chinese-style lyrical piece with vivid imagery.

x00513.d: Watkins's Prayer, a gentle, contemplative piece.

x01093.d: Martinů's first flute sonata, lively and lyrical in Czech neoclassical style. Tests agility and stamina.

x01205.d: Large, ornamented partita in D with overture, allemande, courante, aria, sarabande, minuet and gigue; tests stamina and style.

x01228.d: Pair of Scarlatti sonatas in contrasting moods; practises crisp articulation, hand-crossing and rhythmic energy.

x01275.d: Dutilleux's Piano Sonata: a sinewy Allegro con moto, a song-like Lied and a Choral et variations finale. Rhythmically complex, orchestral in colour, demanding in stamina.

x01392.d: Minimalist work in repeated patterns, unfolding in shifting gate-like cycles; hypnotic and demanding in stamina.

x01393.d: One of the twelve impressionistic Spanish pieces; virtuoso, colourful and hugely demanding.

x01394.d: Piano piece by a Jamaican-British composer; rhythmic and expressive.

x01395.d: Large Russian romantic sonata; passionate and virtuoso.

x01396.d: Polish neo-classical sonata with driving rhythms and a Bartók-like energy.

x01397.d: Busoni's grand piano transcription of Bach's chaconne; monumental and virtuoso.

x01398.d: American sonata with a dramatic first movement and a fiery fugue finale.

x01399.d: Percussive, rhythmic sonata in three movements; Hungarian folk influence.

x01400.d: Romantic, big-boned sonata with sweeping chromatic lines.

x01401.d: Beethoven's heroic sonata with a rippling Rondo finale; virtuoso and dramatic.

x01402.d: Stormy, dramatic sonata with an intense finale; pushes technique and emotional range.

x01403.d: Programmatic sonata depicting farewell, absence and return; dramatic and expressive.

x01404.d: Late Beethoven sonata in A with contrapuntal finale; lyrical and complex.

x01405.d: Late sonata with a radiant variations finale; lyrical and spiritual.

x01406.d: Late sonata with arioso and fugue; deeply expressive.

x01407.d: Final sonata in two movements, fiery and transcendent; Arietta variations.

x01408.d: Set of variations that introduced the Eroica theme; brilliant and playful.

x01409.d: Dense, Romantic one-movement sonata of Second Viennese School; tightly structured.

x01410.d: Four pieces by a Russian-Ukrainian Late Romantic; lyrical and virtuoso.

x01411.d: Fierce, serialist sonata; complex, uncompromising rhythms.

x01412.d: Brahms's first sonata, bold and heroic with a lyrical slow movement.

x01413.d: Passionate sonata in F sharp minor, brilliant and demanding.

x01414.d: Brahms's third sonata, a heroic and lyrical five-movement work.

x01415.d: Early Brahms theme and variations on an original theme; clear, lyrical variations that practise voicing, characterisation and sustained control.
x01415.rw: Lesser-known Brahms; rewarding, less daunting than Handel

x01416.d: Monumental set of variations ending in a grand fugue; demands stamina, polyphonic clarity and wide variety of touch and character.
x01416.rw: Brahms masterpiece; a classic diploma choice

x01417.d: Two books of virtuoso variations on Paganini's Caprice No. 24; relentless technical challenges in thirds, sixths, leaps and octaves.

x01418.d: Bridge's large, dark and intense one-movement-feeling sonata, written in memory of Ernest Farrar; harmonically rich with orchestral piano writing.
x01418.rw: Powerful British sonata, long and demanding, not often heard

x01419.d: Modern British piece with jazz-tinged, banjo-like energy and brittle, spiky rhythms; practises rhythmic precision and colour.

x01420.d: Contemporary British piece with driving rhythms and percussive textures; practises rhythmic control and sharp articulation.

x01421.d: Elliott Carter's late two short pieces (Caténaires and Matribute); intricate polyrhythms, quick shifting textures and spare modern language.

x01422.d: Six concert studies of Romantic character with brilliant figuration and singing melody; practise fluency, evenness and expressive shaping.

x01423.d: Six brilliant modern etudes exploring rhythm, tempo layers and extreme technique; virtuosic and imaginative, in the Ligeti tradition.
x01423.rw: Fresh, exciting modern etudes with real prestige

x01424.d: Chopin's greatest ballade: a long narrative arc with a wistful theme, dramatic climaxes and a fiery coda; tests structure, voicing and stamina.

x01425.d: Dramatic, march-like fantasy with a hymn-like middle and expansive structure; practises long-range planning, rubato and strong chordal playing.

x01426.d: Chopin's visionary late polonaise-fantasy; free, improvisatory form with a shimmering central section and heroic close.
x01426.rw: Profound late Chopin, a celebrated recital piece

x01427.d: The 'Funeral March' sonata: stormy opening, scherzo, famous funeral march and the eerie whispering finale. Practises drama, control and endurance.
x01427.rw: Iconic sonata, hugely recognisable and rewarding

x01428.d: Chopin's grand late sonata, broad and lyrical, with a brilliant scherzo, a glowing Largo and a headlong finale; demands stamina and shaping.

x01429.d: Fauré's early Ballade, a graceful, flowing piece with delicate figuration and a lively central section; practises refined touch and colour.

x01431.d: Franck's three-part piece with a flowing prelude, lyrical aria and a brilliant, cyclic final; cyclic form and big sonority.

x01432.d: Franck's imposing triptych: meditative prelude, chorale and a fugue which brings the themes together; tests polyphonic clarity and big textures.

x01433.d: Ginastera's first sonata, with Argentine folk-inflected rhythms, driving toccata-like energy and a mysterious slow movement; tests rhythm and power.

x01437.d: Henselt's romantic salon studies, rich in wide stretches and arpeggios and singing tune; practise legato, stretches and a poised cantabile.

x01439.d: Liebermann's virtuosic set of four gargoyle pieces; spiky, demonic, vigorous writing with big chords and rapid passagework in a modern idiom.

x01443.d: Ligeti's rainbow etude with luminous, slow-moving harmonies over a flickering line; practises sustained tone and finely graded colour.

x01449.d: Liszt's elegy for the fallen of 1848, with a solemn funeral march, thunderous octaves and a tender central theme; tests octaves and drama.

x01455.d: MacMillan's piano sonata, a taut Scottish-flavoured piece with ritual intensity, folk echoes, spiritual feeling and sharp contrasts.

x01476.d: Clara Schumann's six Soirées musicales, including a Notturno, Mazurkas and a Polonaise; graceful salon pieces that practise voice leading and nuance.

x01484.d: Stravinsky's four-movement neoclassical suite 'in A' (Hymne, Romanza, Rondoletto, Cadenza finala); lean, bell-like and poised.

x01485.d: Szymanowski's three exotic, virtuosic pieces (Scheherazade, Tantris, Don Juan's Serenade), full of colour, rich textures and rhythmic flair.

x01486.d: Three poems after Homer's Odyssey (Isle of the Sirens, Calypso, Nausicaa); delicate, sensuous and finely coloured.

x04560.d: MacMillan's one-movement sonata, rhythmically energetic with Scottish and sacred influences, big climaxes and intricate writing.

x04561.d: One of Frank Martin's Eight Preludes, concentrated pieces with chromatic harmony and contrasting moods.

x04562.d: Rachmaninov's dazzling transcription of Mendelssohn's fairy-light Scherzo, with fleet staccato and delicate textures.

x04563.d: Messiaen's four rhythmic studies (Île de feu 1 and 2, Neumes rythmiques, Mode de valeurs). Complex rhythm and dense textures.

x04564.d: Morel's evocative étude exploring sonority and resonance, with colouristic chords and pedal effects.

x04565.d: Moszkowski's virtuoso études; two are chosen, with brilliant figuration, delicate textures and fast writing.

x04566.d: Mussorgsky's famous suite portraying paintings, linked by the Promenade, ranging from delicate to monumental.

x04567.d: Poulenc's playful transcription of the finale from Le Bal masqué, a sparkling toccata with wit and rhythmic crackle.

x04568.d: Rachmaninov's large set of variations on Chopin's C minor Prelude, a Romantic showpiece with lyrical, dramatic and virtuosic sections.

x04570.d: Reger's imposing variations and fugue on a Bach theme, thick and contrapuntal with marked contrasts of mood.

x04571.d: Rihm's modernist Klavierstück, with sudden contrasts, expressive intensity and extreme dynamics.

x04572.d: Roslavets's early Russian sonata in an advanced post-Scriabin harmonic language, intense and rhythmically complex.

x04573.d: Ginzburg's brilliant transcription of Figaro's Largo al factotum, packed with fast patter, leaps and humour.

x04574.d: Rzewski's virtuosic ballad built on a relentless, mechanical ostinato suggesting mill machinery, steadily building in intensity. Demands stamina, rhythmic drive and control.

x04575.d: Scarlatti's bravura sonata in D, K119, with hand-crossing, repeated notes and Spanish guitar effects.

x04576.d: Schlozer's two virtuoso études, op. 1, in Romantic Russian style with fast passagework.

x04577.d: Schumann's first piano sonata, a sprawling and passionate early Romantic work with contrasting moods.

x04578.d: Schumann's Concert sans orchestre, a stormy, intricate sonata with a theme-and-variations slow movement.

x04579.d: Scriabin's late sonata with dissonant harmony, trills and mystical atmosphere, intensely demanding.

x04580.d: Serocki's Polish preludes, with sharp, modern textures and brief contrasting moods; three are chosen.

x04581.d: Shchedrin's two neo-baroque polyphonic pieces, witty and inventive with strongly contrapuntal textures.

x04582.d: Smetana's tone-poem-like piece depicting Macbeth, dramatic and stormy with strong contrasts.

x04583.d: Two characterful pieces from Smetana's Dreams, one a wistful lament and the other a lively Czech folk festival.

x04584.d: De Kaan's piano transcription of Smetana's Vltava, flowing river theme with folk dances and big climaxes.

x04585.d: Sorabji's brief and intricate fantasy, rich in dense harmony and rhythmic complexity.

x04586.d: Stevenson's festive, colourful piece evoking Scottish Beltane fire rituals, rhythmically strong and decorative.

x04587.d: Cziffra's glittering transcription of Strauss's Tritsch-Tratsch Polka, with rapid repeated notes and sparkling humour.

x04588.d: Godowsky's richly layered, lush paraphrase of Strauss's Wein, Weib und Gesang waltz, full of inventive counterpoint.

x04589.d: Stravinsky's four short etudes from the piano collection, brief and witty modernist pieces.

x04590.d: Stravinsky's jazzy rag for piano, rhythmically spiky, with percussive effects and shifting metre.

x04591.d: Stravinsky's three movements from Petrushka (Russian Dance, Petrushka's Room, The Shrove-tide Fair), a famous virtuosic transcription.
x04591.rw: Landmark showpiece, hugely demanding and popular

x04592.d: Agosti's transcription of Stravinsky's Firebird (Infernal Dance, Berceuse and Finale), a colourful and demanding piano adaptation.

x04593.d: Talma's atonal, intense second sonata, with strongly contrasting movements and dense counterpoint.

x04594.d: Wild's playful virtuoso transcription of Tchaikovsky's Dance of the Four Swans, with fleet staccato and jaunty rhythm.

x04595.d: Villa-Lobos's suite of eight children's pieces, depicting dolls in a range of characters, from lyrical to rhythmically wild.

x04596.d: Vine's powerful first sonata, with energetic rhythmic drive and dramatic Australian modernism.

x04597.d: Vine's dramatic third sonata, a driving work with strong rhythms and intense drama.

x04598.d: Vladigerov's set of Bulgarian folk-based variations on Dilmano Dilbero, with colourful textures and a dance feel.

x04599.d: Weber's brilliant first sonata, with a fast perpetual-motion finale and virtuoso runs.

x04600.d: Weissenberg's lively and nostalgic arrangements of French chanson hits, with pianistic flair and jazzy swing.

x04601.d: Wilkinson's evocative paintings-inspired set of five pieces, Impressionistic and colourful.

y00107.d: Bach's Italian Concerto: a bright Allegro, ornamented Andante and brilliant Presto imitating orchestral contrasts, practising clarity, ornaments and rhythmic drive.

y00108.d: Bach's Prelude and Fugue in A♭ from Book II of the Well-Tempered Clavier: flowing, stately prelude with a graceful fugue, practising voicing and counterpoint.

y00109.d: Beethoven's 'Pathétique' Sonata: dramatic Grave–Allegro, a famous Adagio cantabile and a driving Rondo, practising range of touch, control and contrast.

y00110.d: Beethoven's Sonata in E, Op. 14 No. 1: a bright Allegro, a Scherzo-like Minuet movement and a lively Rondo, practising clarity, touch and Classical phrasing.
y00110.rw: Pleasing but less dramatic early sonata

y00111.d: Beethoven's Sonata in G, Op. 14 No. 2: a graceful, witty sonata with an Allegro, variations Andante and a playful Scherzo, practising clean fingerwork and Classical style.

y00112.d: Mozart's Sonata in B♭, K. 570: an elegant Allegro with flowing runs, a lyrical Adagio and a Rondo, practising Classical phrasing and clean passagework.

y00226.d: Bach's Toccata in G minor, BWV 915: an early work with a free opening, fugal sections and a lively conclusion, practising improvisatory flexibility and counterpoint.

y00248.d: Bach's Partita No. 6 in E minor, BWV 830: a large-scale suite opening with an improvisatory Toccata, practising counterpoint, ornament and stamina.

y00372.d: Bach's Partita No. 2 in C minor, BWV 826. Sinfonia and dances with intricate counterpoint.

y00373.d: Prelude and Fugue in A minor, BWV 865, from the Well-Tempered Clavier Book 1. Intense, with a challenging fugue.

y00374.d: Prelude and Fugue in B minor, BWV 869, from WTC Book 1. Serious, long and expressive.

y00375.d: Prelude and Fugue in F♯ minor, BWV 883, from WTC Book 2. Flowing and lyrical.

y00376.d: Prelude and Fugue in G minor, BWV 885, WTC Book 2. Dramatic prelude and spirited fugue.

y00377.d: Bartók's Suite, Op. 14 (1916). Folk-based, percussive and rhythmically bold.

y00378.d: Beethoven's Sonata in D, Op. 10 No. 3 (1798). Dramatic, with deeply expressive Largo e mesto.

y00379.d: One of Bortkiewicz's Four Piano Pieces, Op. 65. Romantic, rich in texture.

y00380.d: Two Chaminade concert études, Op. 35. Virtuosic, brilliant with Romantic lyricism.

y00381.d: Chopin's Ballade No. 4 in F minor, Op. 52 (1842): a long narrative built on a tender theme, with dramatic climaxes and a fiery coda.

y00382.d: Two movements from Schoenberg's Suite, Op. 25 (1923). A 12-tone work in Baroque dance forms.

y00383.d: One of Clara Schumann's Soirées musicales, Op. 6 (1836). Expressive, brilliant Romantic miniatures.

y00384.d: Robert Schumann's Sonata in G minor, Op. 22 (1838). Impassioned with a fiery first movement.

y00385.d: Scriabin's Etude Op. 8 No. 12 in D♯ minor (1895). Dramatic, thunderous and powerful.

y00546.d: Bach's French Suite no. 4: Allemande, Courante, Sarabande, Gavotte, Air, Menuet and Gigue. Practises ornaments and elegant French style.

y00547.d: Bach's French Suite no. 5: seven dances from Allemande to Gigue, bright and cheerful. Practises ornaments, rhythm and clean articulation.

y00548.d: Praeludium and Gigue from Bach's Partita no. 1 in B flat: flowing, graceful opening and a lively, hand-crossing Gigue. Practises clean fingering.

y00552.d: Handel's Suite no. 8 in F minor: free Prelude and Fugue followed by dance movements. Practises Baroque style and expressive playing.

y00563.d: Bach's dramatic Chromatic Fantasia, with improvisatory runs and arpeggios, followed by a taut fugue. Practises freedom, drama and counterpoint.

y00615.d: Overture from Bach's Partita no. 4 in D: a grand French overture with a fast fugal section. Practises ornaments and rhythm.

y00616.d: Preludes and fugues from Well-Tempered Clavier book 1, chosen from a list. Practises voice-leading, articulation and style.

y00617.d: Preludes and fugues from Well-Tempered Clavier book 2, chosen from a list. Practises voice-leading and style.

y00618.d: Sinfonia, Allemande and Capriccio from Bach's Partita no. 2 in C minor: stately opening, flowing dance and brilliant finale. Practises counterpoint.

y00619.d: Large-scale improvisatory Toccata opening Partita no. 6, with a fast fugal section. Practises counterpoint and stamina.

y00620.d: Bartók's four-movement Suite with folk-like first movement, biting harmony and driving rhythms. Practises rhythm and clarity.

y00621.d: Beethoven's Pathétique Sonata, in three movements: a dramatic Grave, a famous Adagio cantabile and a stormy Rondo. Practises tone, drama and technique.

y00622.d: Beethoven's Sonata quasi una fantasia in E flat, with linked movements and a lively finale. Practises changes of character.

y00623.d: C sharp minor Mazurka (Op. 50 no. 3), a long, melancholic and sophisticated dance, plus the shorter D major Mazurka (Op. 33 no. 2). Practises rubato and rhythm.

y00624.d: Coleridge-Taylor's Romantic setting of the spiritual 'Deep River' from his Twenty-four Negro Melodies: rich chords, a warm singing melody and sustained voicing.

y00625.d: Witty descriptive scherzo with sneaking cat and scampering mouse; practises articulation and rhythm.

y00626.d: Handel's Suite no. 6 in F sharp minor in four movements with a rapid Gigue. Practises fast passagework and ornaments.

y00627.d: Jazz scherzo from New York Nights, with sophisticated rhythm and swing. Practises syncopation and rhythmic control.

y00628.d: Mendelssohn's Prelude and Fugue in F minor, a serious and dramatic pair in Baroque style. Practises counterpoint.

y00629.d: Mozart's Sonata in A, with Theme and Variations, Menuetto and Rondo alla turca. Practises elegance, ornaments and clear style.

y00630.d: Ten variations on Gluck's tune 'Unser dummer Pöbel meint', witty and varied. Practises ornaments and character changes.

y00631.d: Rachmaninov's Preludes nos. 5 (G major) and 12 (G sharp minor): lyrical, then brooding. Practises voicing and rubato.

y00632.d: Scarlatti's Sonatas K 263 (E minor) and K 264 (E): a contrasting pair with fast, crisp lines. Practises articulation and ornaments.

y00633.d: Schoenberg's Six Little Piano Pieces: aphoristic atonal miniatures. Practises delicacy, timing and sound.

y00634.d: Clara Schumann's Romance in A minor, op. 21 no. 1 (1853), a short songful piece; practises singing tone, balance and rubato.

y00635.d: Schumann's Grillen ('Whims'), a capricious character piece with rhythmic twists. Practises rhythm and lively character.

y00636.d: Schumann's Novelette no. 1 in F: a vigorous and rhythmic piece with a calm middle. Practises rhythm and drive.

y00637.d: Schumann's Romance in B: a tender lyrical piece with a singing melody. Practises legato and tone.

y00638.d: Two Scriabin preludes from Op. 11, brief and expressive. Practises voicing and colour.

y00639.d: Four brief Shostakovich preludes: witty, varied and rhythmic. Practises character changes and clarity.

y00640.d: Bach's English Suite no. 2 in A minor: brilliant prelude then dances. Practises ornaments and passagework.

y00641.d: Bach's Partita no. 3 in A minor: seven bright dances beginning with Fantasia. Practises rhythmic clarity.

y00642.d: Preludes and fugues from Book 1, chosen from a list. Practises voice-leading and expression.

y00643.d: Preludes and fugues from Book 2, chosen from a list. Practises voice-leading and expression.

y00644.d: Busoni's piano transcription of Bach's Toccata and Fugue in D minor: grand, orchestral, dramatic. Practises virtuosity.

y00645.d: Barber's four jazz-influenced Excursions. Practises rhythm, syncopation and character.

y00646.d: Beach's Four Sketches: colourful pieces including Fireflies. Practises tone colour and agility.

y00647.d: Beethoven's Tempest Sonata: dramatic, with stormy outer movements and a moving Adagio. Practises drama and control.

y00648.d: Beethoven's 'Hunt' Sonata in E flat: playful and bright. Practises elegance and wit.

y00649.d: Beethoven's Les adieux sonata: Farewell, Absence, Return. Practises expressive depth and drama.

y00650.d: Brahms's Rhapsody in E flat, op.119 no.4: bold, march-like, rhapsodic. Practises chords and character.

y00651.d: Chopin's Barcarolle: a flowing, rocking lyrical work with passionate climax. Practises voicing and pedalling.

y00652.d: Two contrasting Chopin Études from Op. 10. Practises technical mastery and musicality.

y00653.d: Chopin's Polonaise-fantasy: free, improvisatory and dramatic. Practises tone and structure.

y00654.d: Chopin's Variations brillantes on a Hérold theme: brilliant early variations. Practises agility.

y00655.d: Balakirev's transcription of the Romance from Chopin's Piano Concerto no. 1: lyrical and rich. Practises tone and sustained line.

y00656.d: Howard Ferguson's Sonata in F minor: dramatic, lyrical and tightly constructed. Practises control and character.

y00657.d: Peter Racine Fricker's Studies, op. 38: concise modern technical pieces; likely practise rhythmic control and clear articulation.

y00658.d: Ginastera's Danzas Argentinas: three dances (The Old Herdsman, The Graceful Maiden, Dance of the Gaucho). Practises rhythm and colour.

y00659.d: Ginastera's Suite de danzas criollas: five dance pieces. Practises rhythm and character.

y00662.d: Rachmaninov's later set (1916-17): darker, more orchestral than op. 33, with thick chords, fast figuration and pictorial moods. Practises sonority, voicing and stamina.

y00663.d: Preludes from the 1910 set, lyrical (nos. 2, 9, 13) or driving (nos. 6, 8) in Rachmaninov's rich chordal style. Practise voicing, rubato and sonority.

y00665.d: Schumann's op. 1, a theme on the notes A-B-E-G-G followed by light, glittering variations and a closing Finale alla fantasia. Practises finger agility and variety of touch.

y00670.d: Busoni's monumental D minor transcription of Bach's violin Chaconne, giving the variations organ-like fullness and orchestral colour. Practises sustained architecture, voicing and stamina.

y00676.d: Beethoven's F minor sonata: a stormy Allegro assai, a calm variation Andante con moto, and a relentless presto finale. Practises dynamic extremes, control and endurance.

y00677.d: Brahms's 1861 set: twenty-five variations on a Handel aria in B-flat, ending in a grand fugue. Practises variety of character, voicing, big chords and stamina.

y00678.d: Each book gives a theme from Paganini's Caprice no. 24 in A minor with fourteen variations, full of leaps, double notes and octaves. Practises technical bravura and endurance.

y00679.d: Chopin's B-flat minor sonata: turbulent opening, driving scherzo, the famous Funeral March and a whispering unison finale. Practises drama, voicing and control of long structure.

z00201.d: Fast, hopping galop with bouncing staccato in both hands. Practises crisp staccato, quick repeated rhythms and light touch.

z00202.d: A simple folksy song-like melody with gentle accompaniment. Practises cantabile tone, balance of melody and accompaniment, and simple phrasing.

z00203.d: A small early Mozart Allegro in B flat written when he was a child. Two-part writing with simple scales; practises evenness, Classical articulation and phrasing.

z00204.d: Rollicking galloping rhythm in A minor, a famous piece from Album for the Young. Practises rhythmic drive, dynamics and energetic chords.

z00205.d: A lilting Italian-style song with a simple tune over strumming guitar-like chords. Practises phrasing, rubato and balance of melody over chords.

z00206.d: A short graceful waltz in A minor from Grieg's first set of Lyric Pieces. Practises waltz rhythm, light left-hand accompaniment and singing right-hand melody.

z00207.d: Piano arrangement of the lyrical slow movement of Mendelssohn's violin concerto. Practises sustained melodic line, rubato and balance of melody and accompaniment.

z00208.d: Piano version of Grieg's famous creeping-then-furious march. Practises building tempo and volume, staccato control and rhythmic accuracy.

z00209.d: A fast, light toccata-style piece with brisk running notes in alternating hands. Practises finger independence, even tone and quick staccato.

z00210.d: A humorous, stomping little march with bold rhythms and quirky harmonies. Practises sharp rhythm, dynamic contrast and a wit typical of Prokofiev.

z00211.d: Beethoven's late Bagatelle in G minor, quick and stormy in outer sections with a quieter central passage. Practises Classical-Romantic character, fast scales and dynamic shaping.

z00212.d: A graceful, elegant Gavotte in a light dance style, with neat staccato and delicate phrasing. Practises articulation and crisp rhythm in a Classical-flavoured Romantic idiom.

z00213.d: Opening piece of Kinderscenen: a gentle, lilting melody in G major evoking tales of faraway places. Practises singing tone, voicing and flexible phrasing.

z00214.d: A colourful, evocative piece depicting rain turning to a rainbow, with shifting harmonies and textures. Practises tonal colour, pedalling and control of dynamics.

z00215.d: A spiky, lively portrait of grasshoppers hopping in a procession, with quirky staccato and sharp harmonies. Practises precision, rhythmic wit and hand coordination.

z00216.d: A lively Scherzo in G minor by Clara Schumann with leaping figures and rhythmic energy. Practises fast fingerwork, dynamic contrast and Romantic style.

z00217.d: A short, quietly solemn piece from Album for the Young, a chorale-like movement with a hymnlike texture. Practises sustained legato, voicing and even chords.

z00218.d: The Child Falling Asleep from Kinderscenen: a hushed, drowsy piece with delicate harmonies and slowing pulse. Practises tonal control, soft dynamics and sensitive rubato.

z00219.d: The famous Turkish March finale: bright A minor-major rondo with percussive left-hand accompaniment and repeated-note rhythms. Practises finger agility, clear articulation and rhythmic drive.

z00221.d: Second of Clara Schumann's Quatre pièces fugitives: a restless, passionate piece with flowing figures and shifting harmonies. Practises voicing, rubato and Romantic phrasing.

z00367.d: Short descriptive piece with a steady whirring ostinato imitating a sewing machine, from Bonis's children's album. Practises even rhythm, light touch and control of dynamics.

z00368.d: Folk-song-based piece from Bartók's For Children, dark and rhythmic, with a sturdy Hungarian character. Practises rhythmic precision, accents and contrast between sections.

z00369.d: Lilting 6/8 boat-song from Burgmüller's popular studies. Practises a singing right-hand melody over a rocking accompaniment, balance and smooth phrasing.

z00370.d: Short Allegretto from the sketchbook Mozart wrote as a child in London in 1764. Light and clear, practising even finger work, phrasing and simple ornaments in early Classical style.

z00371.d: Gentle lilting Sicilienne in 6/8 from Schumann's Album for the Young. Practises a singing line, rocking accompaniment and a sense of dance-like flow.

z00372.d: The famous C major prelude of broken chords that opens the Well-Tempered Clavier. Practises evenness, voice-leading and shaping harmonic progressions over a steady flow.

z00374.d: Galloping Horseman piece from Schumann's Album for the Young. Practises rhythmic drive, accents and quick, light finger work with strong contrast of character.

z00375.d: Tender, dreamy piece from Tchaikovsky's Children's Album. Practises a cantabile melody over a smooth accompaniment, rubato and careful balance between hands.

z00377.d: Percussive, stamping dance from Bartók's Mikrokosmos, with heavy accents and chords in a folk-like idiom. Practises rhythmic vitality, accents and control of loud dynamics.

z00378.d: Barcarolle-style study from Burgmüller's 18 Characteristic Studies, with a gondola's rocking motion and a singing melody. Practises legato, balance and gentle rhythmic sway.

z00379.d: Quiet, wandering character piece from Grieg's Lyric Pieces, with expressive harmony and a poetic mood. Practises tone colour, rubato and subtle pedalling.

z00380.d: Spanish dance-like Fiesta from Turina's Miniatures, with vivid rhythms and flamenco-inspired colour. Practises rhythmic vitality, crisp chords and brilliant contrasts.

q00006.d: Hawaiian farewell song by Queen Liliuokalani in a gentle, swaying style; practises legato melody, supportive left hand and relaxed phrasing.

q00007.d: Quiet, mysterious piece with sparse texture; practises soft touch, pedal-free legato and sustaining a mood in simple five-finger positions.

q00009.d: Dark, moody piece in a low register with a shadowy character; practises dynamic control, legato and confident hands-together playing.

q00011.d: Cool, bluesy piece with a sleuthing, swaggering feel; practises swung-style rhythm, staccato and a jazzy left-hand pattern.
